draft_context.description: Xiaomi Sound Play review It turns out that major mobile manufacturer Xiaomi also makes Bluetooth speakers, and its latest model, the Xiaomi Sound Play, is aiming to deliver “immersive, powerful sound” as well as a “stylish and versatile” design. But that’s not all. The tech giant is doing all of this while keeping its speaker nice and cheap. It comes in at just £49.90 (about $67 / AU$95) — which is refreshingly affordable for an 18W model with features such as smart lighting, Auracast, and IP68 waterproofing. So can the Xiaomi Sound Play compete with some of the very best Bluetooth speakers around? The answer is a little more complicated than a simple yes or no. Let’s start by looking at the areas in which the Sound Play excels, and there are a fair few of these. I alluded to some a moment ago — its waterproofing and LED lights, for example. That IP68 rating means that the speaker is fully dustproof, but can also survive a dunking under a meter and a half of water for as long as 30 minutes, so you really can take it anywhere without fear of damage. The lighting — a key selling point of this speaker — is pretty neat too. Lights sit on the base of the speaker and beneath a panel on the top side, which resembles an infinity mirror. And the rings of lighting really help to make your listening sessions more immersive, especially in lower-lit conditions. You can customize the color and pattern of the lights too, and one setting also syncs up to bass output. That level of customizability is spectacular to see on a speaker in this price category. More generally, I’m quite a big fan of how the Sound Play looks. It comes in four very stylish colors — the Purple variant I tried is quite the looker, as is the Green version. It is reminiscent of the JBL Flip 7 in terms of look and feel, with a neat fabric exterior and psuedo-cylindrical build. The inclusion of the infinity mirror light and handy rubber strap also make it a real stand-out, looks wise. Another welcome inclusion is a built-in mic, for speakerphone duties. This is something you don't often see these days and it does add value, on paper. However, I made a phone call and although my voice sounded clear on the other end, I noticed a high-pitched chime whenever the other person wasn’t speaking. It wasn’t a dealbreaker (my discussion was still easy to navigate), but it's my job to notice these things. Other highlights include a JBL Grip -rivalling 14-hour battery life — which is excellent for a speaker of this size — as well as Bluetooth 6.0 connectivity, and true wireless stereo playback for anyone with multiple Sound Play models at their disposal. Something that the Sound Play omits, however, is companion app support. For me, this is a bigger miss — an app could’ve opened up EQ adjustment, remote light alteration, and precise battery life tracking. The speaker’s nominal price doesn’t quite excuse this either. There are a number of budget-friendly rivals from the likes of Earfun, Edifier, and Tribit that do come with app support. (Image credit: Future) By now you must be wondering how Xiaomi’s speaker sounds. In honesty, it’s a bit of a mixed bag. It’s a steady performer in some areas, but in need of improvement in others. In general, the Sound Play delivers fairly clear audio. In Yes I Know My Way by Pino Daniele, vocals had good presence in the mix, and even had a decent sense of separation from other instruments in the mid-range. OK, higher-pitched drums weren’t the most expressive or articulate, but they didn’t sound tinny at mid-volume, and bass was weighted relatively well too. With more energetic tracks, such as Trip by Ruze, the cracks started to show. There was a slightly compressed quality to the track, and the pumping bass just didn’t come through with the command or depth of similarly sized rivals, including the JBL Grip, which I directly tested against the Sound Play. During this comparison, the Grip just delivered a more fun performance, with enhanced directionality and low-end punch. But that’s not to say Xiaomi’s speaker was blown out of the water — it still held its own with commendable clarity in the mid-range and fairly agile bass. In House tracks, bass drops didn’t always have the impact or dynamism I was listening out for, and vibrant drums could occasionally sound on the blunt side. But then again, the Xiaomi didn’t succumb to a boomy, super-muddy sound that a lot of its budget rivals do — it puts up a fairly controlled performance overall. As a smaller speaker, the Sound Play can’t get super loud, and bass will thin out substantially at top volume levels. It also won’t deliver the most detailed or open sound ever — again, I found a few tracks sounded a little compressed and narrow, which isn’t helped by the lack of higher-res codecs like LDAC or aptX. (Image credit: Future) All in all, I think the Sound Play sounds good enough for the price you pay. Sure, it’s not the most dynamic or revealing-sounding model on the market, but you get typically clear, decently balanced sound without having to shell out all too much cash. So, looking at the Xiaomi Sound Play as a whole, would I consider it worth buying? Well that depends. If you’re on a tight budget, and you want a speaker for less than £50, then I think the Sound Play is an option worth considering. It doesn’t sound amazing, but it gets the job done, and I’m a big fan of its durable yet eye-catching design. However, if you’ve got a little more money to play with, then I’d suggest picking up the JBL Flip 7. That model can produce truly seismic bass, incredibly clean audio, and has a top-class companion app to boot. The JBL Grip is another neat alternative, especially if you can grab it on sale. (Image credit: Future) Xiaomi Sound Play review: price & release date Priced at £49.90 (about $67 / AU$95) Launched in May 2026 Scheduled to release in Australia in August 2026 The Xiaomi Sound Play was launched in May 2026, at the same time as its recently released 17T series . The speaker is available for £49.90 (about $67 / AU$95) in the UK, although Xiaomi told me that there are no plans for a US release, and the speaker won’t be available in Australia until August 2026. It can be purchased in one of four colors — Black, Green, Purple, or White — via Xiaomi’s digital store. Attribute Notes Score Features Adjustable lighting, good battery life, but lack of app is a shame. 3.5/5 Performance Decently balanced audio with clear vocals, but lacks the depth and dynamism of some rivals. 3.5/5 Design Infinity mirror and lights look great, neat color options, well protected against the elements. 4.5/5 Value Decent enough audio and great design at a very affordable price point. 4/5 Buy it if… You want something stylish I’m a big fan of the way Xiaomi’s Sound Play speaker looks. It comes in a funky range of colors, has personalizable lighting, and the infinity mirror feels like the cherry on top. You’re on a tighter budget Something the Sound Play has over rivals from the likes of JBL and Bose, is that it’s available at an exceedingly low price. At £49.90 (about $67 / AU$95), it’s highly affordable, and although it could sound a little better, I think it easily earns its price. Don’t buy it if… You want the best-sounding speaker Although the Sound Play is a steady enough performer, offering relatively balanced audio output with clear vocals, it’s no sonic marvel. It lacks the extension and authority of similarly powered (and sized) rivals like the JBL Grip and JBL Flip 7 — so if you want truly great audio, it may not be your best option. You’re looking for a speaker with remote controls Perhaps the biggest shame here is that the Sound Play omits a companion app. This would’ve enabled remote control of lighting, EQ, and more, and it’s something that a huge proportion of Xiaomi’s competitors can deliver. When listening to music I mainly streamed tracks over Tidal , but I dipped into Spotify from time to time as well. As always, I started out by sifting through the TechRadar reference playlist , which features songs from a wide variety of genres. I also listened to a ton of tunes from my personal library as well, though. More generally, I’ve spent years reviewing audio gear here at TechRadar, and have tested a whole lot of Bluetooth speakers — more than 50 in fact. I’ve tried out everything from pocket-sized audio companions like the Bose SoundLink Micro Gen 2 through to luxurious large-sized alternatives like the Marshall Bromley 750 , as well as Xiaomi Sound Play rivals like the JBL Grip, so I know exactly what it takes for a speaker to stand out in this highly competitive market. sections.heading: Tác động thực tế với người đọc
sections.body: Điện thoại gập mang lại sự linh hoạt ấn tượng khi vừa nhỏ gọn lại vừa mở ra không gian sử dụng lớn. Tuy nhiên, để thực hiện cơ chế gập mở hàng ngàn lần, màn hình bên trong bắt buộc phải được thiết kế mỏng manh hơn. Sự đánh đổi này khiến tấm nền dẻo trở nên vô cùng nhạy cảm và dễ hư hỏng. Đây cũng chính là yếu tố then chốt ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến tuổi thọ của thiết bị. sections.heading: Chi tiết cần kiểm chứng
sections.body: Hầu hết các mẫu điện thoại gập xuất xưởng đều được dán sẵn một lớp phim bảo vệ dẻo chuyên dụng. Lớp nền nhựa polyimide kết hợp cùng OLED linh hoạt giúp màn hình chịu lực tốt khi gập lại. Nhà sản xuất Samsung khuyến cáo người dùng nên giữ nguyên lớp bảo vệ tích hợp sẵn này. Việc tự ý dán thêm một lớp bảo vệ thứ hai sẽ gây cản trở khớp gập và làm hỏng màn hình. Câu hỏi tiếp theo là tín hiệu này có thành rollout bền vững, thay đổi giá trị sản phẩm, giới hạn đáng chú ý hay chỉ là một nhịp cập nhật ngắn. Phần này chỉ giữ chi tiết có thể kiểm chứng và tránh lặp lại nguyên văn cách diễn đạt của nguồn.

sections.heading: Ai nên hành động hoặc chờ
sections.body: Trái ngược với màn hình chính, màn hình phụ bên ngoài lại hoạt động tương tự smartphone thông thường. Việc dán thêm kính cường lực cho màn hình ngoài là hoàn toàn hợp lý và được khuyến khích. Sự phân biệt rõ ràng giữa hai màn hình sẽ giúp người dùng bảo vệ máy hiệu quả hơn. Với người đọc, khung hữu ích gồm bằng chứng hiện có, nhóm bị ảnh hưởng, rủi ro còn lại và điểm nên kiểm tra trước khi hành động. Phần này cần gọi đúng nhóm độc giả nên hành động ngay hoặc nên chờ thêm xác nhận.

sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp
sections.body: Thực tế, rắc rối với miếng dán dẻo màn hình trong đã xuất hiện ngay từ những thế hệ điện thoại gập đầu tiên. Nhiều người từng sai lầm bóc bỏ lớp phim nhà máy khiến màn hình bị hỏng nghiêm trọng ngay sau đó. Hiện nay, các hãng đã cho phép thay thế miếng dán bảo vệ chính hãng thông qua các trung tâm dịch vụ. Giới chuyên gia cảnh báo người dùng tuyệt đối không nên tự thay thế tại nhà vì nguy cơ hỏng rất cao. Một bài tốt cần tách rõ sự kiện từ nguồn, tác động với người đọc và câu hỏi theo dõi để không giống bản tóm tắt link rời. Phần này nên khép lại bằng tín hiệu cần kiểm tra tiếp, không tóm tắt lại cùng một ý.

sections.body: Người bán hàng trên sàn thương mại điện tử đang từng bước thích ứng với các quy định thuế mới. Ảnh minh họa từ Pexels. Tín hiệu từ GenK Tin ICT cần được đặt vào bối cảnh trước: thời điểm xuất hiện, chi tiết đã có cơ sở và lý do nó đáng nằm trong dòng tin công nghệ hôm nay. Phần này cần dựng lại thay đổi đã có cơ sở trước khi chuyển sang nhận định.

sections.heading: Tác động thực tế với người đọc
sections.body: Ngày 6/8, Tạp chí Tài chính doanh nghiệp phối hợp Hội Tư vấn Thuế Việt Nam (VTCA) tổ chức hội thảo "Quản trị rủi ro thuế thương mại điện tử". Tác động thực tế nằm ở workflow, chi phí, rủi ro hoặc quyết định mua/dùng; Sàn TMĐT gửi sai doanh thu, hóa đơn của người bán cho cơ quan thuế: Ai sai - người đó chịu trách nhiệm nên được giải thích qua lăng kính đó trước khi kết luận rộng hơn. Phần này cần nối câu chuyện với workflow, chi phí, bảo mật hoặc quyết định dùng/mua của người đọc.

sections.heading: Chi tiết cần kiểm chứng
sections.body: Tại sự kiện, độc giả thắc mắc: Trong trường hợp người bán phát hiện doanh thu do sàn thương mại điện tử chuyển cho cơ quan thuế không khớp với doanh thu thực tế, người bán cần liên hệ với sàn hay cơ quan thuế để được xử lý? Quy trình điều chỉnh dữ liệu và trách nhiệm của từng bên được thực hiện như thế nào? Câu hỏi tiếp theo là tín hiệu này có thành rollout bền vững, thay đổi giá trị sản phẩm, giới hạn đáng chú ý hay chỉ là một nhịp cập nhật ngắn. Phần này chỉ giữ chi tiết có thể kiểm chứng và tránh lặp lại nguyên văn cách diễn đạt của nguồn.

sections.heading: Ai nên hành động hoặc chờ
sections.body: Ông Đặng Văn Thành, Phó Chi cục trưởng Chi cục Thuế Thương mại điện tử trả lời: Khi người bán phát hiện dữ liệu doanh thu do sàn thương mại điện tử chuyển đến cơ quan thuế không khớp với doanh thu thực tế, trước hết cần chủ động liên hệ với sàn thương mại điện tử để rà soát, đối chiếu và xác định nguyên nhân phát sinh sai lệch. Với người đọc, khung hữu ích gồm bằng chứng hiện có, nhóm bị ảnh hưởng, rủi ro còn lại và điểm nên kiểm tra trước khi hành động. Phần này cần gọi đúng nhóm độc giả nên hành động ngay hoặc nên chờ thêm xác nhận.

sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp
sections.body: Trường hợp xác định có sai sót trong dữ liệu đã kê khai, sàn thương mại điện tử có trách nhiệm thực hiện kê khai bổ sung, điều chỉnh theo đúng quy định của pháp luật về quản lý thuế, đồng thời cập nhật lại thông tin đã gửi cho cơ quan thuế. Một bài tốt cần tách rõ sự kiện từ nguồn, tác động với người đọc và câu hỏi theo dõi để không giống bản tóm tắt link rời. Phần này nên khép lại bằng tín hiệu cần kiểm tra tiếp, không tóm tắt lại cùng một ý.

draft_context.source_title: TerraMaster F4-425 Pro NAS review: Very fast, with backup, surveillance, and media streaming galore
draft_context.description: Macworld At a glance Expert's Rating Pros Affordable for four bays Dual 5Gbe connections Tons of apps and capabilities Excellent performance Unlimited IP cams in surveillance app Cons Drive trays don’t lock Requires mail address during initialization TOS 7 still slightly buggy Our Verdict TerraMaster’s F4-425 is a fast, versatile, four-bay storage, backup and media streaming NAS box that’s every bit as good as, if not better than similar units from QNAP and Synology. Especially as the company doesn’t gouge you for IP cam licenses. Price When Reviewed This value will show the geolocated pricing text for product undefined Best Pricing Today Price When Reviewed $639 Best Prices Today: TerraMaster F4-425 Pro Retailer Price $699.99 View Deal $699.99 View Deal TerraMaster $800 View Deal Price comparison from over 24,000 stores worldwide Product Price Price comparison from Backmarket I’m always surprised how few people own a NAS (Network Attached Storage) box such as the highly capable F4-425 Pro reviewed here. NAS requires a bit more tech savvy than cloud services and storage, plus some upfront cost, but there’s one particular reason it’s worth it: complete and private control of the apps, services, and most importantly –the data you store on it. Internet outage? Doesn’t affect your NAS. Online data breech? Doesn’t affect your NAS. Monthly payments? Only to your power company. Simply put, NAS is fantastic for data backup and streaming media about the house and can also serve as the engine for a home surveillance network. We like NAS, and TerraMaster has quickly become one of our favorite consumer flavors thanks to excellent hardware and apps, a newly faster OS, and the lack of surcharges vendors such as QNAP and Synology hit you up with for things such as additional IP cam licenses. That said, there was the occasional immaturity in the apps and operating system. What are the F4-425 Pro’s features? The F4-425 Pro is a silver and black hued, mostly metal, four-bay NAS box with quick swap, non-locking 3.5-inch drive trays. It measures approximately 7.1-inches wide by 8.6-inches deep, by 5.9-inches tall and weighs around 6.5 pounds bare. That will of course increase as you add drives. If you remove the four screws on the bottom holding the aluminum body to the chassis, you’ll find three PCIe 3.0 NVMe M.2 slots that accept NVMe SSDs. There’s enough space for heat sinks, which would be a good idea to prolong SSD life. Note that you can use PCIe 4.0/5.0 SSDs but they’ll be limited to PCIe 3.0 speed. The front of the unit provides access to the four drive bays, as well as the power button and a single 10Gbps USB Type-A port. The back is home to an additional pair of 10Gbps Type-A USB ports, twin 5Gbe Ethernet ports, and HDMI port (console use only), and a single Type-C port for diagnostics and the like. There’s also the power jack, a pinhole reset button, and a rather massive exhaust fan. The back of the F4-425 Pro with its dual 2.5Gbpe and 10GBps Type-A ports. There’s a Type-C port but it’s only for diagnostics. The HDMI port is for console (command prompt) use only. The processor inside of our test unit was a capable 8-core Intel N350 with a substantial 16GB of DDR5 onboard. That’s plenty of power for advanced tasks like virtual machines and Docker. TerraMaster also provides several apps for backup up mobile devices, and even controlling the box. The TNAS mobile app on install and first use. TerraMaster provides 2-year warranty on the F4-425 Pro. And thankfully, the company now also provides a downloadable PDF user’s guide. How is the F4-425 Pro’s setup? Adding drives to the tool-less trays is largely painless: slide them out, pop out the side rails, slip in the 3.5-inch HDD and replace the side rails. Screws are provided for 2.5-inch hard drives or SATA SSDs. As described above, you’ll need to remove the outer shell to access the three PCIe 3.0 NVMe slots. lWhen you first boot the F4-425 (and most TerraMaster NAS) it presents a dialog asking for your email address to receive a code. That’s of course after you find its IP address (E.g. 192/168.1.110) and visit with your browser. Below the email field, in very light lettering, is the ability to bypass this step. If you choose, you can activate your online presence with TerraMaster during setup. Alas, you still have to enter your email. I don’t like sending info to a company until I’m very familiar with the hardware and said company. I wish TerraMaster would abandon this practice ad to be blunt–it’s none of their darn business. To be fair, you can put the F4-425 Pro into “Security Isolation Mode” (Control Panel / Security/ Security Isolation Mode) after setup, to prevent any further traffic outside of your local network. The F4-425 also features a highly configurable firewall if that’s too drastic a measure for you. What is the F4-425 Pro’s operating system and software like? The F4-425 Pro delivered our first look at the latest version 7 of TOS (TerraMaster Operating System), a substantially feature-equivalent but far better-performing version of the operating system (version 6) than I tested with the F2-425 . Especially in regards multitasking. Beyond that, it appeared to me to be more evolutionary than revolutionary, despite heralding itself as the first AI-enabled NAS OS. It does allow you to install OpenCLAW which enables normal language access to various features. TerraMaster says OpenCLAW makes things easier, but the real issue with most new NAS users is that they don’t know what to ask, let alone how to ask it. Actually, thinking about it, that’s the issue with just about any AI system. Note also that the minute I opened OpenCLAW, the F4-425 Pro’s fan kicked into high gear. It takes some juice. That said, I quite like TOS, it’s as well laid out as the QNAP and Synology equivalents, and perhaps a bit more intuitive. However, I found version 7 a bit buggy. Rough around the edges, as it were. I stuck with TOS 7 as it’s so much quicker at everything than version 6 but there were some annoyances such as the inability to include spaces in a backup job name, and not automatically resuming jobs that were not completed in the last session. I’d also be careful doing searches and deleting the results with the file manager. There are also tons of apps for backup, surveillance, development, and multimedia streaming. Below is my favorite: Centralized Backup, which can back up from numerous sources (SMB, FTP, etc.) without the need to install clients on every machine. Simply share the folders or files you want across the network, locate them and create a job to back them up. I love Centralized Backup’s ability to back up my shared folders without me having to install client software on the involved computers. Centralized Backup, along with CloudSync (back up to a host of online services) are my favorite TOS backup apps, but there are quite a few others (Duple Vault, Elephant Drive, etc.) as well as TerraMaster’s own client-based, portal driven TerraSync. There’s also a handy folder mirroring utility (TFM) that you can use across volumes. eAll the backup and sync options offered by TOS 7. Want to keep tabs on your house? TerraMaster includes Surveillance Manager (shown below), which offers support for unlimited cameras. This is in distinct contrast to Synology and QNAP which limit you to one or two cameras so they can sell you more licenses. This is one of the best reasons to opt for a TerraMaster NAS box, however, note that you’ll have to configure your router to reach the app remotely. The Surveillance Manager opens in a separate tab and allows up to tk IP cams. While I use TOS’s DLNA Multimedia Server to stream movies to my TV, TerraMaster also includes the extremely popular Plex (shown below), as well as Jellyfin and Emby for fans of those systems. The extremely popular Plex Media Server is present in TOS 7. TRAID is TerraMaster’s hybrid RAID solution (all NAS vendors have one these days) that combines mirroring (RAID 1) and parity (RAID 5). It allows you to combine drives of different sizes while using more of their capacity than standard RAID modes do. Generally speaking, most RAID modes allow you to use only the capacity of each drive in the array equal to that of the smallest drive in the array. Combine a 4TB HDD and an 8TB HDD in RAID 0 (striping) or RAID 1 (mirroring), and only 4TB of the 8TB drive is used, while the rest just sits there. TRAID and similar solutions let you employ the otherwise wasted capacity as another volume, or part of one. How much is the F4-425? The F4-425 Pro with the Intel N350 retails for $799, but was on sale at TerraMaster’s site for $639 at the time of this writing. From TerraMaster’s Amazon store make that $699. There’s a cheaper $569 Intel N305/8GB version of the F4-425 Pro available, as well as less endowed $599 F4-425 Plus (Intel N150 processor, 16GB), and $429 F4-425 (quad-core, 4GB) models if the Pro is too pricey for you, or you don’t need to run VMs, Docker, etc. The Plus and plain versions were discounted to $480 and $344 respectively at the time of this writing. All use the same operating system and offer the same applications. The F4-425 Pro’s price is roughly on par for a NAS box with this grade of processor, 16GB of memory and NVMe slots, but as always — shop around, though we’re fairly sure you’d be happiest with the TerraMaster. How does the F4-425 perform? The F4-425 Pro features dual 5Gbpe (Multi-gig) so it’s capable of nearly 600MBps when using that protocol, and around 1GBps if you aggregate the two 5Gbps Ethernet adapters. At 2.5Gbps, expect around 290MBps, and on gigabit, around 140Mbps. There’s no Wi-Fi, but that’s not the best way to use a NAS box. You can with some (and an add-in card), but commonly NAS is connected via Ethernet directly to a router or switch. I populated the F4-425 with a single 1.92GB Seagate IronWolf SATA SSD and two Crucial T710 PCIe 5.0 NVMe SSDs (running at PCIe 3.0 speed) and formatted with the Btrfs file system. All those SSDs are massively faster than 5Gbpe or even 10Gbpe. paragraphs: TerraMaster’s F4-425 is a fast, versatile, four-bay storage, backup and media streaming NAS box that’s every bit as good as, if not better than similar units from QNAP and Synology. Especially as the company doesn’t gouge you for IP cam licenses.

I’m always surprised how few people own a NAS (Network Attached Storage) box such as the highly capable F4-425 Pro reviewed here. NAS requires a bit more tech savvy than cloud services and storage, plus some upfront cost, but there’s one particular reason it’s worth it: complete and private control of the apps, services, and most importantly –the data you store on it.

Internet outage? Doesn’t affect your NAS. Online data breech? Doesn’t affect your NAS. Monthly payments? Only to your power company. Simply put, NAS is fantastic for data backup and streaming media about the house and can also serve as the engine for a home surveillance network.

We like NAS, and TerraMaster has quickly become one of our favorite consumer flavors thanks to excellent hardware and apps, a newly faster OS, and the lack of surcharges vendors such as QNAP and Synology hit you up with for things such as additional IP cam licenses.

The F4-425 Pro is a silver and black hued, mostly metal, four-bay NAS box with quick swap, non-locking 3.5-inch drive trays. It measures approximately 7.1-inches wide by 8.6-inches deep, by 5.9-inches tall and weighs around 6.5 pounds bare. That will of course increase as you add drives.
